S. 1. Special Branch Station File No.................... Date February 6., 1942.

SUBJECT: Release of Communist Suspect

Further to Special Branch report dated
February 2nd, 1942.

At 4 p.m., 5-2-42, on the instructions of
D.C. (Crime) and Major Goto, D.C., the suspect,
Hsu Tsao Sih (許爪雪), alias Hsu Wen Kwei
(許文魁), alias Hsu Yung Kwei (許荣奎),
27, Ningpo, S/unemployed, residing 109 Park Road,
arrested on 21-1-42 at this address, on suspicion
of being concerned in communistic activities, was
released on conditions as stated in the previous
report. He was handed over to one of his
guarantors, Yang Wen Sieu (楊文秀), residing
557 Honan Road.

A further report will be made on receipt of
result of inquiries as to activities of suspect
whilst in Manchukuo, and of the final disposal of
the seized property.

主题：释放共产党嫌疑犯

继1942年2月2日的特务科报告之后。

1942年2月5日下午4时，根据刑事处副督察长（D.C. (Crime)）及后藤（Goto）少校、副督察长（D.C.）的指示，嫌疑犯许爪雪（Hsu Tsao Sih），又名许文魁（Hsu Wen Kwei），又名许荣奎（Hsu Yung Kwei），27岁，宁波人，职业无，居住于公园路109号，该人于1942年1月21日在上述地址因涉嫌参与共产主义活动被捕，现按前次报告所述条件予以释放。他被移交给其担保人之一杨文秀（Yang Wen Sieu），居住于河南路557号。

待收到关于嫌疑犯在满洲国期间活动的调查结果，以及查获财物的最终处理结果后，将另行提交报告。

S.I., Special Branch Station. File No.................... Date February 2, 1942.

SUBJECT: Enquiries into the activities of Suspected Communist arrested in raid on 21/1/42

Further to Special Branch report dated
22/1/42 concerning raid on premises situated at 109
Park Road, suspected to have been used for Communistic
activities and the arrest of a suspect who is being
detained for enquiries.

Enquiries were continued by the undersigned,
D.S. Binks and D.S.I. Loh Wei-kong.

The suspect, Hsu Tsao Sih (許爪雪) alias
Hsu Wen Kwei (許文魁) alias Hsu Yung Kwei (許榮奎),
age 27, Ningpo, S/unemployed, residing with his Mother
Hsu Loh Sze (許樂氏), who is insane, and his
Grandmother Loh Zung Sze (樂鄭氏) at 109 Park Road,
was arrested during a Special Branch raid on the
21/1/42 at this address, when a quantity of books were
seized for further examination. He was brought to
Headquarters for interrogation and is being detained
whilst enquiries are proceeding.

A further examination of the books showed that
although the majority of them are by Russian writers and
some of them deal with affairs in Russia prior to, during
and after the Revolution, they are of the type that are
publicly exposed for sale, and therefore no great
importance can be attached to the possession of them.

主题：调查1942年1月21日突袭行动中逮捕的共产党嫌疑犯的活动

继1942年1月22日关于突袭位于公园路109号处所的特务科报告之后，该处所涉嫌被用于共产主义活动，并逮捕了一名正在拘留接受调查的嫌疑犯。

下述签署人、警佐宾克斯（D.S. Binks）及巡官罗伟刚（D.S.I. Loh Wei-kong）继续进行了调查。

嫌疑犯许爪雪（Hsu Tsao Sih），又名许文魁（Hsu Wen Kwei），又名许荣奎（Hsu Yung Kwei），27岁，宁波人，职业无，与其患有精神病的母亲许乐氏（Hsu Loh Sze）及祖母乐郑氏（Loh Zung Sze）居住在公园路109号，于1942年1月21日特务科突袭该地址时被捕，当时查获了一批书籍以供进一步检查。他被带至总部进行审讯，并在调查进行期间予以拘留。

对书籍的进一步检查显示，虽然其中大多数为俄国作家所著，且部分涉及革命前、革命期间及革命后的俄国事务，但这些书籍属于公开出售的类型，因此拥有这些书籍并不具有重大意义。

It was learned that a number of persons were

to prove the visits were concerned with Communistic

Enquiries are being made as to the activities

Pending the arrival of information as to the

Proprietress of the Nyi Yuan Ziang Rattan Ware Shop
(義源祥籐店), 557 Honan Road, and Lee Kwang Hsi
(李光熙), Proprietor of the Lee Tuh Da Metal Ware Shop
(李德大五金号), 157 Avenue Road, which guarantees are
attached herewith.
The Japanese Authorities also require that
certain of the seized books be handed over to them for
confiscation, the remainder of the books may, however,
be returned to the suspect.
Although, from enquiries made, and the type of
books which the suspect was in possession of, it would
appear he had Communistic leanings. no substantiative
evidence was obtained that he had been actively engaged
in Communism. In view of this. it is respectfully
suggested that he be released on the aforementioned
conditions.

My name is HSU TSAO SIH, alias HSU WEN KWEI
( 許文魁 ) alias HSU YUNG KWEI ( 許榮奎 ), age 27.
I am a native of Ningpo, unmarried, residing at 109 Park
Road with my grandmother-in-law (Loh Zung Sze 梁郭氏 )
and my mother (Hsu Loh Sze 許樂氏 ). My father Hsu
Pao Sung ( 許宝生 ) died in December, 1929, my mother
is insane.

At the age of seven, I commenced study at the
Tien An Dong Primary School ( 天安堂 ), Shantung Road.
After three years, I went to study in the Polytecnic
Public School established by the Shanghai Municipal Council
at Kwangse Road. I studied for about six years in the
latter institute until I was sixteen years of age when I
left the school because of financial difficulties. I
joined the Commercial Radio Company ( 廣西無線電公司 ),
corner of Ningpo and Kiangse Roads and served in the
capacity of an apprentice. Owing to business depression,
the company closed down in May, 1935 and therefore I was
thrown out of employment. I was dependent on my grand-
mother-in-law (Loh Zung Sze) who is the tenant of House
109 Park Road.

After I left the Commercial Radio Company, I studied
English for about 1½ years and Japanese for half a year in
the Liang Zai Vocational Supplementary School ( 量才業餘
補習學校 ) established by the Shun Pao Newspaper Office at
the Tsze Zoh Building ( 慈淑大樓 ), Kiukiang Road.
I also self-studied French in the daytime.

我叫许爪雪，又名许文魁（HSU WEN KWEI），又名许荣奎（HSU YUNG KWEI），27岁。
我是宁波人，未婚，与我的外祖母（梁郭氏 Loh Zung Sze）和母亲（许乐氏 Hsu Loh Sze）居住在公园路109号。我的父亲许宝生（Hsu Pao Sung）于1929年12月去世，母亲患有精神病。

七岁时，我开始在山东路的天安堂（Tien An Dong）小学读书。三年后，我进入工部局在江西路开办的公立工科学校学习。我在该机构学习了约六年，直到十六岁时因经济困难辍学。我加入了位于宁波路与江西路转角的广西无线电公司（Commercial Radio Company），担任学徒。由于商业萧条，该公司于1935年5月倒闭，因此我失业。我依靠我的外祖母（乐郑氏 Loh Zung Sze）生活，她是公园路109号房屋的承租人。

离开广西无线电公司后，我在九江路慈淑大楼（Tsze Zoh Building）由申报馆创办的量才业余补习学校（Liang Zai Vocational Supplementary School）学习了约一年半的英语和半年的日语。
白天我也自学法语。

In February, 1937, I secured employment in the
Lido Ballroom, Medhurst Road, and served as an accountant
in the Confectionery Department. I worked for about four
years until the end of April, 1941 when I proceeded to
Manchukuo for the purpose of attending the funeral
procession of my aunt (Ma Zung Sze 馬鄭氏 ). My grand-
mother-in-law went there one week before I left. I applied
to the Japanese Consulate-General in Shanghai for a "wuchao."
Armed with a "wuchao" issued through the Japanese Consulate-
General, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the National
Government (Nanking), the Commercial Representative Office
of Manchukuo and the Japanese Naval Attache's Office, I
proceeded to Tsingtao by s.s. "Tsingtao" Maru. Having
obtained a "pass" from the Labour Association ( 勞工協會 )
at Tsingtao, I left after one day's stay by s.s. "Dairen
Maru" for Dairen where I proceeded to Fu-shun ( 撫順 )
by train. I arrived on May 3, 1941.

Three days after my arrival at Fu-shun, my aunt died.
My uncle Ma Loo Fang ( 馬魯芳 ) died about one year ago.
He was the partner of the Tien Mur Zung Silk Shop
( 天茂盛 ) at San Fan Ting ( 三番町 ), Fu-shun.
I stayed for about 1½ months in my aunt's home, Yung An Li
( 永安里 ), San Fang Ting, after which I returned to
Shanghai with my grand-mother-in-law.

I have been unemployed since my return to Shanghai
in the middle of June, 1941. I am partially dependent on
my grandmother-in-law and assist in maintaining myself by

1937年2月，我在麦赫斯特路（Medhurst Road）的丽都舞厅（Lido Ballroom）找到工作，在糖果部担任会计。我工作了约四年，直到1941年4月底，我前往满洲国参加姨母（马郑氏 Ma Zung Sze）的葬礼。我的外祖母在我离开前一周去了那里。我向日本驻上海总领事馆申请了“吴超”（wuchao，音译，指通行证或许可）。持有一张经由日本总领事馆、国民政府（南京）外交部、满洲国商务代表处及日本海军武官处签发的“吴超”，我乘坐“青岛”丸轮船前往青岛。在青岛从劳工协会获得“通行证”后，我停留一天，随后乘坐“大连”丸轮船前往大连，再乘火车前往抚顺。我于1941年5月3日抵达。

arrested for being communists while I was taken into custody

买卖香烟和金属制品来维持生计。大约三个月前，我以600.00美元的价格购买了十打中国锁。两周后，这批货物由我的外祖母以700.00美元的价格卖给了二房客庄根（Ding Keng，音译，原文此处中文名与上文徐定根拼音不符，依原文译出）。由于后者既未付款也未归还货物，我与庄根之间发生了纠纷。在丽都舞厅监工袁根发（Yuan Keng Fah）的协助下，纠纷得以解决，庄根的姐夫向我支付了700.00美元的货款。大约两个月前，当庄根试图袭击我时，我们之间发生了争吵。我相信我是因庄根唆使下的诬告而被捕。

My name is Chin Shiao Tung. I am a native of
Nanhwei (南滙), age 28, residing at Lane 279 (Tsing
Foh Li 晉福里), House 31 Rue Ratard. After graduating
at the age of 20 from the Kiangnan Middle School (江南中
學校), King Sze Doo Miao, off Connaught Road, I secured
employment as a teacher in the junior class of the Wu Pei (沪北)
Middle School, previously located at North Szechuen Road,
O.O.L. Following the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese
hostilities in 1937, I was thrown out of employment and
therefore I returned to my native place. In July, 1940,
I came to Shanghai with my wife Tsang San Chuen (張娟)
and three children, and took up residence at the front
upstairs room in the 1st floor, Lane 279, House 31 Rue
Ratard at a monthly rental of $36.00. I first served as
a mathematic teacher in the Hwa Tung Girls' Middle School
(華東女中), Lane 462, House 2 Avenue Joffre. In the
latter part of 1941, I became an instructor in the Ming Lih
Middle School (民立中學), 414 Weihaiwei Road which
position I continue to hold.
I became acquainted with Hsu Tsao Sih (許众雪),
about one year ago. I met him through the introduction of
one Woo Kwan Wen (胡関文) alias Ah Jing (阿勤)
who is a boy in the employ of the Lido Ballroom, Medhurst
Road and a neighbour of my mother-in-law (She resides at
207 Zien Ka Tong (錢家堂), Route Vallon). I learned
that Hsu Tsao Sih was an accountant of the Confectionery
department of the Lido Ballroom and was unemployed about
the middle of 1941. Hsu resides with his mother and

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE SPECIAL BRANCH No. N. 1418 Date 22/1/42）
S. 1, Special Branch Station File No. Date January 22, 1942.
SUBJECT: Raid on premises suspected to be concerned in Communistic activities
At 2.30 p.m., 21-1-42, the undersigned together with D.S. Binks, D.S.I. Loh Wei-kong and C.D.C. 243 raided the top two rooms of premises situated at 109 Park Road, which Rooms premises were, from information received, being used for Communistic activities.
One bundle of books in English and one bundle in Chinese were seized, together with various papers, for further examination. List attached herewith.
The occupant of the rooms, one Hsu Tsao Sih (許瓜雪), alias Hsu Wen Kwei (許文魁), alias Hsu Yung Kwei (許榮奎), 27 Ningpo, S/unemployed, to whom the seized property belongs, was brought to Headquarters for enquiries, and on instructions of Major S. Goto, (D.C.) is to be detained pending completion of the enquiries.
Further report follows.
